title: Impact of Epileptiform Abnormalities on Functional Phenotype in a Cohort of Autism Spectrum Disorder Patients With or Without Epilepsy: A Monocentric Retrospective Study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and epilepsy frequently co-occur, suggesting shared neurobiological underpinnings. While no specific seizure type or epilepsy syndrome is consistently associated with ASD, Epileptiform Abnormalities (EAs) are commonly observed in affected individuals, though their clinical significance remains unclear.
METHODS: This study examined the impact of EAs and epilepsy on the functional phenotype of 338 individuals with ASD, assessed through video-EEG (v-EEG) and standardized psychometric tools (ADOS-2, Leiter-R, WISC-IV, VABS).
RESULTS: Results showed that ASD individuals with epilepsy exhibited significantly lower cognitive performance compared to those with ASD alone or with EAs. Additionally, greater symptom severity was observed in the ASD-+EA group. However, no significant differences emerged in adaptive functioning or language abilities.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the potential influence of epileptiform activity on cognitive and behavioral outcomes in ASD. Further longitudinal research is warranted to elucidate the prognostic implications of EAs in ASD and better characterize its impact on functional profile.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF AUTISM AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS
